Bill.BriefDescription: Concerning employee meal and rest breaks.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to meal and rest periods; and adding a new sectionto chapter 49.12 RCW.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 49.12 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) Employers must allow employees a thirtyminute meal break, onthe employee's time, if the employee works five or more consecutivehours. Meal breaks must begin no less than two hours or more than fivehours from the beginning of the shift. Meal breaks are on theemployer's time when the employee is required by the employer to remainon duty on the premises or at a prescribed work site in the interest ofthe employer. (2) Employers must allow employees working three or more hourslonger than a normal work day at least one thirty-minute meal breakprior to or during the overtime period. (3) Employers must allow employees a rest break of ten minutes, onthe employer's time, for each four hours of working time. Rest breaksmust be scheduled as near as possible to the midpoint of the work p. 1 HB 2737period. Employers may not require employees to work more than threehours without a rest break. (4)(a) Where the nature of the work allows employees to takeintermittent rest breaks equivalent to ten minutes for each four hoursworked, employers may obtain a waiver of the scheduled rest breakrequirements of subsection (3) of this section from the director. Thedirector shall develop by rule a process for employers to apply forwaivers from the department. (b) An employer that allowed employees to take intermittent restbreaks before or on the effective date of this section may continue thepractice while the employer applies for a waiver from the department.Starting on July 1, 2012, however, an employer must obtain a waiverfrom the department to substitute intermittent rest breaks for thescheduled rest breaks required under subsection (3) of this section.
